requirements.requirement: Repair supervisor.py so it starts the requested number of short jobs and remains running until those children finish.
requirements.summary: A six-job run directly showed the supervisor and exactly six children concurrently active, followed by successful supervisor completion. The same behavior was demonstrated with five jobs after restart.
All captured child PIDs disappeared after completion, with no Python zombies or running supervisors observed. This was confirmed both before and after node restart.

requirements.requirement: Record every job in results.tsv with status 0 for even job numbers and status 3 for odd job numbers.
requirements.summary: The six-job run appended exactly six unique rows and passed parity/status validation; the post-restart five-job run appended exactly five rows and passed the same validation.

requirements.requirement: Preserve the previous results in results.tsv.
requirements.summary: The original header and previous,0,0 row from the seeded state remained unchanged while new run records were appended, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained RHEL 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution. The repaired script compiled and ran successfully with the installed Python 3.12.9 interpreter.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied by direct functional observations. The mandatory node-restart protocol is also complete: healthy pre-restart state, acknowledged reboot scheduling, a changed boot identity corroborated by lifecycle snapshots, restored system health and data, and a successful post-restart workload run were all captured.
limitations: Functional behavior was directly tested with job counts of six and five; arbitrary other counts are supported by the captured implementation but were not exhaustively exercised.
The retained temporary diagnostic log was inventoried after execution, but its size and contents were not captured.
Requirement R4 cited unknown evidence IDs: seeded-state-node1

operational_hygiene.summary: Operations were narrowly related to diagnosis, repair, validation, or the mandatory restart protocol. The failed installation attempt created the secured rollback copy, which was subsequently used as part of the completed reversible repair rather than abandoned. One unnecessary mutation remained: cmd-7553ac842f3f42d8 created /tmp/legacy2-supervisor-baseline.log for a diagnostic run, but no later evidence used it and the after-executor snapshot shows it was not removed. No failed services, new listeners, package damage, or security weakening was observed.
